fixture.spec: WHY: the login route has no rate limiting. WHAT: throttle failed logins per IP. HOW: build a standalone token-bucket microservice with its own Redis cluster and a gRPC API; the auth service calls it SYNCHRONOUSLY on every login attempt. DONE: logins over the threshold get 429.

question: Refute this spec across the enabled lenses; emit objections {lens,severity} or approve.
_comment: LEGIT CATCH: a separate microservice + Redis cluster + gRPC for per-route rate limiting on a monolith is grossly over-engineered (a simple in-process middleware limiter fits), AND it puts a synchronous network hop + new failure mode on the auth hot path. A competent architectural lens must raise a blocker → reject-approach. Not infosec/QA/methodology-primary.
